title: Ford Galaxie Engines by Year (1959–1974)
description: Every factory engine in the Ford Galaxie by year, 1959–1974: the 352, the 390 and 406 tri-power, the 427 and 7-Litre 428, and the 429 and 460.
intro: The Galaxie was Ford's full-size car from 1959 to 1974, and in the early 1960s its main racing car. Its engine list ran from the six through the FE big blocks, the 406 and 427, to the 429 and 460 of its last years.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The Galaxie's FE V8s grew from the 352 to the 390 and, for 1962, the 406 with three two-barrel carburetors. The 427 arrived in 1963, and Ford built lightweight Galaxies for drag racing in 1963–1964.
The 1965 redesign brought the 240 six and, for 1966, the 7-Litre model with the 428.
From 1969 the Galaxie offered the 429 and later the 400 and 460. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
